schemaHistory: 1.0 named the fields `reachedAndAttested` and `rejected`. 1.1 renamed the second to `reachedButUnattested`, because `rejected` read as 'not reached'. 1.2 renames the first to `reachedAndAttested`, on Sol's fourth-pass ruling: BOTH fields hold newly reached surfaces, so `reachedAndAttested` implied a contrast with the other field that does not exist. Each is a SHAPE change and not an append, so the version moves both times — the match-behavior benchmark holds at 1.0 through case appends for the opposite reason. Nothing outside tests/lab-match-behavior.test.mjs consumes this fixture.
question: Which word surfaces does comparing denylist entries and passage tokens as STEMS newly reach, beyond what the literal `entry` / `entry + s` tests already reached — and which of those are surfaces a real source could actually contain?
ruling: These, and this file is the vocabulary the answer is exhaustive OVER. Read `reachedAndAttested` + `reachedButUnattested` for what the comparison reaches; read `reachedAndAttested` alone for the part of it a source could actually contain. The v2.6.1 release report published this census twice as 'enumerated over all sixteen entries' and it was wrong both times: the first version named `pays`, which does not match, and omitted SEVEN surfaces (`hosters`, `networkers`, `clouding`, `payable`, `payed`, `serviceable`, `careers`) — an earlier draft of this ruling said six while naming seven, the same by-eye counting error one level up; the second version omitted `carefulness` and `medicalization`; the third omitted `internetization` and `networkization`. Sol found each set. Both failures were the same step — a candidate space generated mechanically and then filtered to real English BY HAND, where a hand that forgets a word leaves no trace. So the hand judgments are now the fixture. `tests/lab-match-behavior.test.mjs` regenerates the mechanical space from the stemmer's own suffix inventory and requires every candidate in it to carry an explicit verdict here, which is what makes an omission impossible rather than merely unlikely.
notExhaustiveOver: English. A surface is only in this file if the stemmer's suffix rules generate it from an entry or an entry's stem, so an irregular form reaching the same stem by another route would not appear — `paid` is the known example and it does not match anyway. Claims of exhaustiveness are about the generated space, never about the language.
twoFieldsTwoKindsOfClaim: THE REACH SET IS reachedAndAttested + reachedButUnattested, AND IT IS MECHANICAL. Every candidate in this file stems to its entry's stem, so the shipped comparison disqualifies every one of them today; that half is complete over the generated space and is not a matter of opinion. `attested` is the second, separate question — whether a real source could contain the surface — and it is a judgment that stays revisable. Moving a word between the two fields therefore changes NOTHING about what the instrument does or what this census claims to reach. It changes only which part of the widening is expected to be met in practice. Three review rounds were spent contesting word calls as though they bounded the reach; they never did, and the earlier field name `rejected` invited exactly that misreading.
wordStandard: For `reachedAndAttested`: listed in a standard English dictionary, or in settled technical use in the register the entry comes from. Arguable calls are recorded rather than applied silently, so a reviewer contests one word instead of the whole table, and they resolve toward the wider stated cost. Arguable and counted as attested: `hosters`, `payed`; `hostable` and `networkable`, added on Sol's second review; and `cloudable`, added on the third — Cisco's IBSG SMB cloud research uses "cloudable" spending for IT spend suitable for cloud delivery, which is settled enough for this register even though the scare quotes in the source show it began as a coinage. Everything in `reachedButUnattested` is still REACHED; it is only unlikely to appear in real text. Added on the fourth review: `internetization` (Passaris' economics coinage — IGI Global carries a dictionary entry, Springer's Journal of International Entrepreneurship uses it in a title) and `networkization`, which is the THINNEST attestation in this file: it is held on the reviewer's two citations, and an independent search surfaced `network-centric` and `networking` instead, so it is the verdict most likely to be wrong next. CONTESTED AND HELD: `softwareization` stays unattested. The reviewer offered ITU and ETSI, but the term those bodies use is `softwarization`, which strips to `softwar` and is NOT REACHED by this denylist at all. The reached spelling and the attested spelling are different words, and that pair is the cleanest demonstration in this file that reach and attestation are independent axes.

bases: each base with no suffix at all
generator.suffixSource: The alternations inside stemToken's own `.replace(/(?:…)$/u, …)` chain in js/lab-analyzer.js, extracted from the source text by tests/lab-match-behavior.test.mjs and asserted equal to the list above. This list is therefore not a second copy that can drift: a suffix added to stemToken and not here fails the suite. It previously WAS a copy, and carried `er`, which stemToken does not strip — Sol's second review caught it. Dropping `er` changed no candidate, because nothing it generates survives the stem filter (`hoster` stems to `hoster`).
variants: the base with a final y replaced by i
generator.variantsSource: Generator convention, NOT a stemToken rule. stemToken maps a trailing `ies` to `y`; the y-to-i variant is how this generator produces the surfaces that rule accepts (`energies`, `utilities`). Declared rather than derived, because it is the one part of the space the stemmer's own text does not give.
generator.keep: candidates whose stem equals the entry's stem, excluding the entry itself and `entry + s` (both already reached by the literal tests)

entries.note: Multiword entries are matched as a contiguous run of two stems rather than as one token, so a single-surface census does not describe them. Their widening is a property of token SEQUENCES and is frozen as the branch truth table in tests/lab-match-behavior.test.mjs — `healthfulness carefulness` and `healths careers` are the sequences the stem run reaches and the literal and substring tests do not.
As `health care`. `childfulness carefulness` is the decisive sequence.
